title: Lift and heat pump efficiency
question: Does the daily COP fall with the temperature lift?

issues.text: Cold days have both a larger lift and more defrost cycles; the house sets the flow temperature through its emitters.
issues.fix: Compare within houses (bins step) as well as across them, and read the Carnot fraction for what the lift alone does not explain.

issues.text: Days of one house are not independent (same installation, same controls).
issues.fix: Read the across-house difference (season step) as four cases, not a sample.

alternatives.question: Within one house, is COP lower on days with a higher flow temperature at the same outdoor temperature?
alternatives.why: Drill down: separates weather compensation from the weather.

alternatives.question: Do houses with underfloor heating have a higher SCOP across all of heatpumpmonitor.org?
alternatives.why: Expand: the public list (system/list/public.json) and yearly stats of hundreds of systems.

hypotheses.statement: The daily COP decreases as the lift (flow − outdoor temperature) grows.
hypotheses.null: COP does not change with the lift.

hypotheses.statement: The daily COP increases in proportion to the Carnot COP.
hypotheses.null: COP does not change with the Carnot COP.

concepts.label: Coefficient of performance
concepts.description: Daily heat delivered / electricity used for space heating.

concepts.label: Temperature lift
concepts.description: Mean flow temperature minus mean outdoor temperature, K.

concepts.label: Carnot limit
concepts.why: The ideal against which the share is read.

method.summary: Regress daily cop on lift_k (H1) and on cop_carnot (H2) over the four houses' days; the fit step gives the least-squares slopes and correlations.

steps.title: Fetch a year of daily stats per house
COP, lift and Carnot per day
steps.detail: days step: cop, lift_k, cop_carnot, carnot_fraction.

steps.title: Fit
steps.detail: fit step: cop_per_kelvin_lift, eta_through_origin, r_lift, r_carnot.

steps.title: Accept or reject H1 and H2
steps.detail: Then repeat with more houses from the public list.

caveats: Four self-selected, well-monitored houses (owners who publish data tend to optimise).
Space heating only; hot water (higher lift) is left out.
Outdoor temperature is the house's own sensor, often in the sun or near the unit.
Low-load days cycle more; defrost is not separated.
